title: Word Classes and Sentence Types (KS2)
subject: English
strapline: The building blocks of grammar and the four sentence types.
facts: Nouns name things; verbs are actions or states; adjectives describe nouns; adverbs describe verbs (often how something is done).
A pronoun replaces a noun: he, she, it, they, we — so you don't repeat the name.
A conjunction joins clauses: and, but, so, because, although, when.
A preposition tells you position or time: under, behind, after, during, above.
A statement tells you something; a question asks; a command tells you to do something; an exclamation shows strong feeling (starts with What or How).
A clause has a verb; a main clause makes sense on its own, a subordinate clause does not.
Adverbs often end in -ly (quickly, carefully) but not always (soon, well, fast).

quick_quiz.q: Name the conjunction in "I ran because I was late".
What type of sentence is "Shut the door."?

teacher_tips: Teach word class by how a word is working in the sentence, not a fixed label.
Colour-code clauses to show main vs subordinate.
Reserve "exclamation" for What/How sentences — a common SATs trap.
